title: ～ほど — to the extent of ～
summary: Shows how far a condition goes by giving an example of the extent. In 'tired to death' the exaggeration conveys a high degree. It follows the plain form of a verb or adjective, or a noun.

patterns.gloss: Plain form / い-adj / noun + ほど

body.p: '～ほど + predicate' says the predicate is true to the extent of what comes before. Extreme examples are common: 死ぬほど, 涙が出るほど, 立っていられないほど.
Often interchangeable with くらい／ぐらい, but ほど is a little more polite and bookish. With numbers it means 'about': 十人ほど. ほど～ない (comparison) is a separate pattern.

examples.ja: 死（し）ぬほど疲（つか）れました。
立（た）っていられないほどお腹（なか）が痛（いた）い。
examples.romaji: Tatte irarenai hodo onaka ga itai.
examples.tr: My stomach hurts so much that I can't stand up.

examples.ja: 涙（なみだ）が出（で）るほど笑（わら）った。
examples.tr: I laughed so hard that tears came out.

pitfalls: 死ぬほど does not mean someone actually dies. It only stresses the degree.
Use the plain form before ほど: 出るほど, not 出ますほど.
